title: Sr. Manager, Assembly, Integration & Test, Project Sunrise - Orbital Data Centers
text:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Advanced Concepts and Enterprise Engineering (ACE), supporting Blue Origin’s mission of millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. The team fosters innovation and drives engineering workflows of the future, shared solutions and standards, simplicity and lower costs, and manufacturable design.

**About the Program**
---------------------

Project Sunrise is designing and building orbital data centers — spacecraft that run AI compute workloads on 100% solar power in orbit. This is a first-of-kind program at the intersection of spacecraft engineering and hyperscale GPU infrastructure, housed within Blue Origin. We are building the team from scratch and need people who can operate at the frontier of both domains.

 

**About the Role**
------------------

his is a leadership role with technical depth: you will manage and develop people, and also own integration and test technical content yourself, alongside senior individual contributors who report to you. You have led spacecraft integration and test through qualification and into production, and you want to do it again with a new kind of payload, a tighter schedule, and a team you get to shape from the start. You will work side by side with Manufacturing, Systems Engineering (verification), the technical leads for the spacecraft bus, compute system, software, and operations. You will represent Assembly, Integration & Test in Program leadership forums and reviews.

 

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Build and lead the Assembly, Integration & Test organization: hire and develop integration and test engineers, technicians, and automation and test data specialists, set clear ownership, and scale the team as the program moves from qualification to production

* Own the integration and test schedule and facility resource allocation: sequence qualification and acceptance campaigns, balance competing demands for chambers, shakers, and test benches, and surface schedule risk early

* Own test anomaly resolution: set the process for stopping safely, preserving evidence, finding root cause, and dispositioning nonconformances, and close anomalies with the design and systems teams

* Plan facilities and equipment: define the space, power, cleanroom, environmental test, and ground support equipment needs, and make build, buy, or lease decisions on schedule

* Drive the design the production flow from first-article integration through repeatable acceptance, with defined stations, handoffs, and test gates that Manufacturing and Operations can run

* Drive test automation: set the architecture for electrical ground support and automated test equipment, and deliver more than 80% automated acceptance testing

* Own the test data and digital thread: make sure results are captured, stored, and traceable to requirements, configuration, and hardware serial numbers, and that they flow to engineering, quality, and operations

* Work with Systems Engineering to implement the verification plan: make sure test configurations, procedures, and readiness reviews support requirement closure, and give test feasibility feedback into requirements and design

* Partner with the spacecraft bus, compute system, and software teams so designs can be integrated and tested, building test access, telemetry, and interface needs into the design early

* Manage relationships with suppliers and external test houses: define scope, schedule, and acceptance criteria, and bring the program's integration and test standards to supplier reviews

* Support the production readiness maturity checklist with objective evidence from integration and test

* Set the safety culture on the factory floor and in the test cell, including hazardous operations review and safe handling, and build a team that stops work without hesitation when something looks wrong

 

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, physics, or a related technical field; master's degree preferred

* 12+ years of spacecraft integration and test, or comparably complex hardware test, experience, including ownership of spacecraft-level qualification or acceptance testing

* Prior experience leading and developing engineers and technicians as a manager, lead, or chief test engineer

* Demonstrated experience running a test schedule and test facilities for flight hardware, including environmental test (vibration, thermal vacuum, EMI/EMC) and the resource trade-offs that come with it

* Experience resolving test anomalies and nonconformances on flight hardware through root cause and closure

* Experience with test automation, including electrical ground support equipment and automated test equipment, and with test data management and traceability

* Experience establishing or substantially improving integration and test processes, facilities, or tools in a fast-moving environment

* Ability to make and defend sound technical decisions with incomplete information, and to communicate clearly with engineers, executives, suppliers, and customers

 

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Experience taking a spacecraft from first-article integration to production-rate acceptance testing, including converting manual procedures to automated test

* Experience with high-power or high-heat-flux spacecraft, or with high-density electronics, HPC, or GPU hardware in demanding environments

* Experience planning and commissioning new test facilities or major environmental test equipment

* Experience managing external test houses or test suppliers, including scope, schedule, and quality oversight

* Hands-on experience with digital engineering and manufacturing execution or test data systems, including linking test results to configuration and requirements

* Experience on commercial or rapid-development programs, and judgment in tailoring heritage standards to what a program actually needs

* Experience supporting launch site operations or on-orbit commissioning

 

**Additional Information**
--------------------------

* U.S. citizenship or permanent residency required (ITAR)

* Travel may be required up to 15% of the time but may change based on project needs.

* Relocation assistance available.

 

Base Pay Range for:

VA applicants is $171,093.00 - $239,529.15
CO applicants is $157,318.00 - $220,244.85
WA applicants is $171,093.00 - $239,529.15

**Other site ranges may differ**

 

**Culture Statement**

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 

**Export Control Regulations**

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 

**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical 

 

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
* Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws.

 

**Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation**

Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.
